journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

attempts.failure: Invalid proposal schema: edits.1: Unrecognized key: "keystrokes"

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component (via vanilla-calendar-pro's inputMode keyboard handling) intercepts Tab keydown on the input element and calls preventDefault(), blocking default browser focus movement to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown event listener on the input element that detects Tab key, hides the datepicker calendar, and allows default browser behavior (focus movement) to proceed without preventDefault. Clean up the listener on dispose.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key now moves focus from departure date field to passengers field as expected in standard form navigation, restoring keyboard accessibility for form traversal per WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: Minimal - only affects Tab key behavior when datepicker is shown
Arrow key navigation within calendar remains intact
verification_requirements: Arrow keys still navigate calendar dates when open
Escape still closes calendar (existing regression guard)
Form submission works with entered values

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component (via vanilla-calendar-pro's inputMode keyboard handling) intercepts Tab keydown on the input element and calls preventDefault(), blocking default browser focus movement to the next form field. The previous fix used a bubbling-phase listener which runs after VCP's handler, so preventDefault() had already been called.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown event listener on the input element that detects Tab key, stops propagation to prevent VCP's handler from running, hides the datepicker calendar if shown, and allows default browser behavior (focus movement) to proceed without preventDefault. Clean up the listener on dispose.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key now moves focus from departure date field to passengers field as expected in standard form navigation, restoring keyboard accessibility for form traversal per WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: Minimal - only affects Tab key behavior on datepicker input elements
Arrow key navigation within calendar remains intact
Capture-phase listener runs before VCP's handler, preventing its preventDefault()
verification_requirements: Arrow keys still navigate calendar dates when open
Escape still closes calendar (existing regression guard)
Form submission works with entered values
